q: Are emissions from a tractor I hire with its driver Scope 1 or Scope 3?
title: Hired tractor emissions: which scope?
short: Scope 3. A tractor hired with its operator from a custom hiring centre or a neighbour is run by them, so its diesel is in their Scope 1 and your Scope 3, Category 1, as a purchased service. Only tractors you own, or lease and operate yourself, are Scope 1.
audience: Farmers, FPOs and agri companies using custom hiring centres

p: Under operational control, a source is Scope 1 if you run it day to day: you drive it or employ the driver, and you maintain it. A hired tractor with its operator fails that test for the farmer.

ul: Tractor hired with operator: Scope 3, Category 1.
Tractor rented without operator, driven by you: Scope 1 under operational control.
Combine harvester hired per acre: Scope 3, Category 1.

p: Hours or acres worked and the diesel used, from the hiring centre's log. Without litres, estimate from hours and label it an estimate.

example.title: Worked example: hired ploughing (illustrative inputs)
lines: Ploughing hired from a custom hiring centre: 8 hours
Diesel used, from the centre's log: 40 litres
40 x 2.68 = 107.2 kg CO2, reported in Scope 3, Category 1 (purchased service)
example.note: Hours and litres are illustrative; 2.68 kg CO2 per litre is the IPCC 2006 diesel default.

senseible: Senseible reads the invoices behind each line and files them as Scope 1, Scope 2 or Scope 3 evidence; the scope choice for contracted services follows the control test you record in your method note.
